extracted.intended_audience: UVA Magazine readers (alumni, students, university community); readers interested in journalism ethics
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating the reporting, editing, and fact-checking standards applied in a long-form investigative journalism piece (here, the Rolling Stone 'A Rape on Campus' article) and the failures identified by a journalistic review. Focus is on routine journalistic practices, editorial oversight, and post-publication corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek comment from people criticized / basic fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: “Journalistic practice—and basic fairness—require that if a reporter intends to publish derogatory information about anyone, he or she should seek that person’s side of the story.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reporter plans to publish derogatory information about individuals, they must seek that person’s side. Example failure: Erdely did not seek to find the three friends Jackie described unflatteringly; had she contacted them she would have heard at least one contradictory account. Anti-pattern: publishing unflattering allegations without attempting to reach or quote the people implicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give organizations adequate chance to review and respond
rubrics_metrics.description: Erdely “did not give Phi Kappa Psi, where the assault was alleged to have taken place, enough of a chance to review and respond to Jackie’s full allegations.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before publishing claims about an organization or group, provide them the opportunity to review full allegations and respond; doing so may reveal discrepancies and prompt further verification. Anti-pattern: presenting incomplete allegations to an organization and publishing without allowing a substantive institutional response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify identities and alleged connections
rubrics_metrics.description: Erdely “never located the student Jackie said orchestrated her sexual assault—a lifeguard named Drew... There was a person named Drew at the aquatic center... but he did not belong to Phi Kappa Psi ... and police have found no evidence linking him to Jackie’s assault.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters must locate and verify named individuals and the connections claimed in a story (membership, employment, role). Failure to confirm identities or links is a substantive factual error. Guidance: check institutional rosters, employment records, and corroborating testimony; seek corroboration with independent evidence or authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial oversight: insist on more reporting, travel, time
rubrics_metrics.description: “Investigative reporters working on difficult, emotive or contentious stories often have blind spots. It is up to their editors to insist on more phone calls, more travel, more time, until the reporting is complete. Woods did not do enough.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors are responsible for recognizing reporters' blind spots and demanding additional verification—more calls, on-the-ground reporting, and time for fact-checking—until the reporting is complete. Scoring note: strong editorial oversight requires proactive checks, challenge of assumptions, and insistence on corroboration before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corroborate key allegations with independent evidence and multiple sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The Columbia report concentrated on failures to follow “basic, even routine journalistic practice” including missed opportunities to corroborate Jackie’s account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serious allegations—especially about crimes—should be corroborated by multiple independent sources or documentary evidence (police reports, witnesses, records). Anti-pattern: relying primarily or solely on a single source’s unverified account for central claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt, specific retraction and named apologies; hold people accountable
rubrics_metrics.description: Rolling Stone used the report to officially retract its story... Eramo criticized that the magazine’s apology was “half-hearted generalized” and “did not apologize to anyone by name... Rolling Stone has refused to hold anyone accountable.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When errors are confirmed, publications should promptly retract or correct the record, issue specific apologies naming those harmed where appropriate, and take clear accountability (disciplinary or corrective actions). Anti-pattern: delayed retractions, vague/apparent PR-motivated apologies, and absence of accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid false depictions that damage reputations and impede public good
rubrics_metrics.description: UVA President: “Irresponsible journalism unjustly damaged the reputations of many innocent individuals and the University of Virginia... Such false depictions reinforce the reluctance sexual assault victims already feel about reporting their experience.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists must be mindful that inaccurate reporting can harm individuals’ reputations and undermine broader social efforts (e.g., addressing sexual violence). Criterion: weigh potential harm from publication errors and take extra care with sensitive topics. Scoring: higher scrutiny for stories that could stigmatize victims or falsely accuse the innocent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate portrayal of institutional responses and support services
rubrics_metrics.description: Assistant Dean Nicole Eramo assailed the article’s “false and grossly misleading portrayal of the counseling and support” she provided to Jackie.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not misrepresent the actions, motives, or services provided by institutional actors (counselors, administrators). Verify descriptions of support offered and include context; consult the staff involved and document their actions to avoid misleading portrayals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness in correcting online content and honoring removal requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Eramo noted Rolling Stone finally removed the article from its website (something we asked for months ago) only after the Columbia report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When parties request removal of demonstrably false or harmful content, publications should act in a timely manner. Delays in correcting or removing false online content prolong harm and undermine trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct transparent internal review of reporting, editing, and fact‑checking failures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Columbia Graduate School of Journalism reported on the failings of the Rolling Stone article; the report investigated each point in the reporting, editing and fact‑checking processes for the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News organizations should undertake clear, public reviews of editorial processes when significant failures occur, identifying specific points of breakdown in reporting, editing, and fact-checking, and publishing findings so readers can assess remediation steps.
